messages:
lina: starting quantus-9b bring-up notes. ran targeted evals across retrieval vs non-retrieval prompts, multistep reasoning, and slot-filling. posting the smoke metrics + initial routing idea.
marco: drop the numbers pls.
lina: paste below (small synthetic / sampled prod slice):
``
variant | quant | retrieval | avg EM | MRR@5 | p95 latency | cost / 1k tok
quantus-9b-fp16 | fp16 | on  | 0.82   | 0.91  | 128ms | $0.052
quantus-9b-int8 | int8 | on  | 0.80   | 0.89  | 106ms | $0.038
quantus-9b-int6 | int6 | on  | 0.73   | 0.81  | 85ms  | $0.028
quantus-9b-int6 | int6 | off | 0.78   | 0.86  | 80ms  | $0.028
```
lina: notes: int6 loses most on retrieval-anchored EM (entity disambiguation) but is closer on pure generation. int6 with retrieval disabled recovers ~5% EM vs retrieval-on cases, suggesting indexing context interacts with quant errors.
emily: interesting. so int6 is fine for non-retrieval or short completions. what's the delta on perplexity / NLL?
lina: NLL delta (int6 vs fp16) on retrieval-on tasks ~+0.45 nats, on retrieval-off ~+0.12. multi-step reasoning sequences have higher delta and long-context recall drops.
ryan: product will ask about downstream impact. can we express as %requests impacted at different severity thresholds?
marco: quick pass: severity buckets we used — minor (formatting/noise), moderate (incorrect but plausible entity), major (wrong legal/financial fact). tag counts from sample: minor 3.8%, moderate 4.5%, major 1.2% of requests on retrieval-on traffic. overall ~9.5% regressed in some way on int6.
emily: yikes. do we have priming/mitigation tests?
lina: ran a light-touch mitigation: 2x template priming (repeat short anchor sentences) and a retrieval-postfilter that checks top-k token overlap. results: priming recovers ~40% of moderate errors (moderate -> minor) and reduces major by ~30%. combined with postfilter (cheap token-scoring) we can detect ~60% of remaining majors and route them to fp16. latency impact for those that stay on int6: +10ms median; for ones routed to fp16 fallback cost+latency applies.
ryan: ops question: how much extra token tax does priming add? what's the cost math for expected fallback fraction?
marco: calc: priming adds ~4 tokens on average -> cost_add = 4 * (0.028/1000) = $0.000112 per call on int6. fallback to fp16 (when postfilter triggers) adds delta cost roughly $0.024 per 1k tokens on that call (assuming same length). break-even if fallback frequency > ~0.0047 (~0.47%). i.e. if priming avoids >0.5% of fp16 fallbacks per call it's worth it vs always fallback.
emily: product guidance request: thresholds where int6 is acceptable. suggestion: use int6 when expected user-value-per-call < $0.005 and request intent in {short-summarize, casual-chat, formatting}. keep int8 default for high-value intents (legal, billing, search-answers).
lina: ops routing draft:
- default: quantus-9b-int8 (balance).
- conditional fast-path: quantus-9b-int6 when (tokens_out <= 64) AND (retrieval_context_overlap_score < 0.2) AND (intent in fast_intent_list).
- priming: apply 2x priming for int6 when intent in {short-summarize, faq} and run postfilter; if postfilter indicates low overlap confidence or hallucination signal > threshold, escalate to int8 or fp16.
- canary plan: shadow int6 for 7 days at 2% traffic, collect severity labels and NLL deltas, then scale to 10% if major errors < 0.5% and overall regression < 5%.
ryan: ops note: int6 deployment shows occasional p95 jitter under large batching windows. recommend batch_window_ms = 12 for int6 and a lower max_batch_tokens. also enable KV cache alignment checks for long-context retrieval.
emily: sample failure (sanitized) we will include in the product brief: 
``
user: who is listed as the invoice recipient for order #9932 in the latest doc?
int6: The invoice recipient is "Northpoint LLC".
fp16: The invoice recipient is "Northpoint Logistics Inc." (correct).
```
emily: proposed handoff artifacts for GTN/product: CSV of top 200 regressed requests, code snippet for postfilter (token overlap heuristic), pass/fail criteria for canary, and a one-page cost-vs-quality heatmap.
lina: I'll open a short doc and tag product/gtm. action items: 1) marco run 7-day shadow at 2% with logging of severity labels; 2) emily prepare product heatmap + threshold recs; 3) ryan ops: set batch_window_ms and enable KV alignment alert; 4) dev: implement lightweight postfilter + priming flag.
ops-bot: canary job scheduled: shadow quantus-9b-int6 @ 2026-04-02T09:00:00Z for 7d at 2%.
marco: noted. will kick off after lunch and post interim results in 48h.
lina: thanks all. goal is to have a final recommendation + routing rules in the onboarding folder after the 7d shadow.
